_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live. Since #2996 a citation that names a `#N` must name an issue that is still OPEN: the gate reads `gh issue view` for every currently-lit alarm's citation and flags a dead reference, because a citation string is not an owner (measured 2026-08-22: 4 of 7 entries pointed at closed issues, 3 of them on lit alarms). A citation with NO `#N` is never flagged by that check — a dated, self-clearing state is honestly cited in prose — but the 14-day `issueless_ancient_reds` rule still forces a `#N` past that tenure. PRUNE an entry when its alarm recovers. Since #3258 a citation may not assert a recurrence NEGATIVE ("no recurrence since", "has not recurred") unless the same note names how it was derived — the log group it was read from, or the query that read it (filter-log-events / describe-alarm-history / start-query). A recurrence-negative is unfalsifiable from the registry alone, and the measured instance hid a live recurrence for four days: this alarm's entry read "fixed by #3066/PR#3075 …, no recurrence since" while the identical finding fingerprint 539c6d sat in /aws/lambda/life-platform-qa-smoke inside the last 72h. Enforced offline against the committed file by tests/test_check_alarm_citations.py::test_the_live_registry_carries_no_underived_recurrence_negative (scripts/check_alarm_citations.py::unfalsifiable_negatives), so it runs on every PR rather than only at wrap. A POSITIVE claim needs no marker — it is checkable by looking.

token-alarm-genesis-window-active.citation: dated self-clearing window, expires 2026-08-24 — no issue, by design
token-alarm-genesis-window-active.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996): the previous citation #2116 closed 2026-08-07 'partial'. This alarm is CORRECT and needs no owner: `lambdas/common/token_alarm_window.py` sets TOKEN_ALARM_GENESIS_WINDOW = ('2026-08-16', '2026-08-24'), a dated window around the cycle-14 genesis (2026-08-17), and the 1/0 gauge is 1 for its duration by construction. Deliberately prose rather than a `#N` — filing an issue for a designed, dated state would be manufacturing an owner for something that is working. If it is still lit after 2026-08-24, that IS a defect and needs one.

cost-metric-drift-sustained.note: Expected RED from ~7 days after its first deploy: the alarm states a true, known condition. Re-measured live 2026-08-24T23:59Z governor cycle (most recent at time of check): ratio 1.3710 — lowest since 08-21, continuing the slow pullback from the 1.4177 peak on 08-22/23, but still ~19% above the 1.15 bar; 19 consecutive 8h datapoints since box 2 landed (08-19) are ALL above bar, none sub-1.15. CE reconciliation re-measured 2026-08-25: Bedrock UnblendedCost $83.32 MTD vs self-reported LifePlatform/AI EstimatedCostUSD $61.36 MTD, a $21.96 gap (26.4%) — down $0.75 from the prior $22.71/27.4% reading a day earlier. The golden-eval AiCostTelemetry grant (previously staged) is now CONFIRMED APPLIED live (aws iam get-role-policy shows the statement; simulate-principal-policy returns allowed for cloudwatch:PutMetricData/LifePlatform/AI; infra/iam/README.md updated) but has not yet moved the ratio — golden-brief-eval.yml runs weekly (next 2026-08-31) and no run has executed since the grant applied. The dominant unattributed residual remains interactive Claude Code dev-session usage (out of scope per #3070's design — never reaches the ADR-062 chokepoint), still unsized. The alarm itself (cost-metric-drift-sustained, operational_stack.py, #2948) was re-audited this pass and found already correctly configured — threshold/window/routing all verified against DRIFT_RATIO_BAR, no alarm-side change needed. Remove this entry when box 2 lands the ratio < 1.15 for a full week AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

budget-tier-sustained-7d.note: RE-CUT 2026-08-23 (#2989, chose Option A over Option C): threshold moved from tier >= 1 sustained to tier >= 2 sustained in cdk/stacks/monitoring_stack.py — merged but NOT YET DEPLOYED (this worktree cannot cdk deploy). ADR-133 derived the permanent $150 base FROM a measured steady state ($4.12/day = 82.4% of $150) that lands inside band 1 (73-87%), so a threshold=1 alarm fired continuously on the platform's DESIGNED steady state from 2026-08-12 (17+ consecutive days) — the same background-noise failure #1927 was filed to prevent, one band up. Band 2 (reader narratives paused) is not the designed state at ~81% MTD spend, so a full week pinned there is genuinely rare and worth answering; #1927's own amendment already moved the two CI gates out of band 1, leaving only five internal/dev features there. EXPECTED POST-DEPLOY: this alarm should clear once `cdk deploy LifePlatformMonitoring` ships the new threshold, because live BudgetTier has not sustained >= 2 for a full week. Re-read the live CloudWatch alarm state after that deploy — if it has NOT cleared, that is new information (tier has been at 2+ longer than assumed here) and this entry should stay with an updated note; if it HAS cleared, prune this entry once it has been OK longer than the #2912 72h flap window.

qa-smoke-warnings.citation: reset-predictable, self-clearing: the sole non-chronic warning is `mcp:get_todoist_snapshot: No Todoist data available`, caused by the cycle-15 wipe (13:15 PT 2026-08-31) removing that day's Todoist record AFTER the day's ingestion had already written it. Todoist pulls 1x daily at 14:00 UTC, so the next run (07:00 PT 2026-09-01) gap-aware-backfills 08-31 and the warning clears. Expiry: if still lit after the 2026-09-01 14:00 UTC ingestion, file an issue.
qa-smoke-warnings.note: Re-cited 2026-09-01 (Session P) because the previous citation's stated REASON had rotted, not merely aged. It read 'a real Withings scale gap ... that the reader-truth judge correctly flags on /api/vitals' — that was the failures side of the pair, and the /api/vitals reader-truth finding turned out to be a bug in the check rather than a true claim (#3401). Derived, not remembered: LifePlatform/QaSmoke::WarnCount Maximum by day = 0.0 (08-28), 0.0 (08-29), 2.0 (08-30), 1.0 (08-31), against ChronicWarnCount 8/7/11/11 over the same days — so the alarm is firing on genuinely non-chronic warnings, and the 2026-08-31T19:36 PT run's log carries exactly one: the Todoist dispatcher line. DDB USER#matthew#SOURCE#todoist newest key is DATE#2026-08-30, confirming the missing 08-31 record. Cadence (14:00 UTC daily) and the 72h staleness bound are read from source_registry.py, not hand-stated.

weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.citation: arming transition of the #2820 dead-man 2026-08-21 — not a delivery failure
weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.note: Kept 2026-08-22 (#2996). The alarm is OK, but #2912's flap check reads a 72h window and this alarm's only episode is inside it: describe-alarm-history shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> ALARM at 2026-08-21 20:44 PT and ALARM -> OK at 21:44 PT — one hour, immediately after #2820 deployed the WeeklySignalSent dead-man (treat_missing=BREACHING, so a freshly created alarm with no datapoints is ALARM by construction until the first one lands). No signal was missed. THE PRUNE RULE, corrected: remove a recovered alarm's entry once it has been OK for longer than the flap window (72h), not the moment it clears — pruning on recovery alone trades a stale entry for a flap-gate red, which is what happened while writing this. Prune after 2026-08-24 21:44 PT if still OK.

budget-tier-unreadable.note: New alarm (2026-08-23, DIL-036 slice of #2824): fires when budget_guard logs BUDGET_TIER_UNREADABLE on the public site-api-ai path — the SSM budget-tier read failed (ParameterNotFound / AccessDenied / outage), website_ai is failing CLOSED (readers get the honest 'paused' output), and the rest of the fleet is running fail-open with NO ceiling enforcement. Never a routine state: if lit, restore the SSM param/grant (/life-platform/budget-tier) — the guard recovers within one 5-min cache TTL. Prune this entry only if the alarm is retired; while #2824 is open it is the named owner.

Expiry: if it fires on a NON-dev day, investigate fresh.

ai-tokens-platform-daily-total.note: RE-POINTED 2026-08-28 (Session I). The previous note read 'dated self-clearing window — expires 2026-08-26T00:00Z'. That window expired and the alarm did NOT clear, so the citation was asserting a self-clearing property the alarm no longer had — the citation was stale, not the alarm. Re-derived from the metric rather than from the note: AWS/Bedrock-derived LifePlatform/AI::AnthropicOutputTokens daily Sum over 2026-08-23..08-26 reads 191765 / 106231 / 195560 / 167974 against a 150000 threshold (GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold). It is a GENUINE sustained breach, not a stuck alarm: three of the last four days are over the line. Cause is the same elevated AI spend #2801 governs — measured Cost Explorer unblended $5.74/day (sd $4.32, n=25, 2026-08-01..08-25), of which Bedrock is 61.8%. #2801 is OPEN and stays open (2 of its 4 boxes met by the 2026-08-28 ceiling re-derivation; the CloudWatch EMF estate inventory and the secrets-manager floor are not). EXPECTED CLEAR: not from this ceiling change — the ceiling moves the tier ladder, not the token volume. This alarm clears when daily output tokens fall below 150k, or it is re-thresholded against the real steady state. PRUNE when the alarm goes OK.

prediction-gradable-share-low.citation: deliberate arming transition (lit 2026-08-26), clearing by DILUTION rather than by the _retire_ungradeable mechanism its own CDK comment names — re-derive at the next wrap; issueless_ancient_reds forces a #N by 2026-09-09
prediction-gradable-share-low.note: ADDED 2026-08-28 (Session I). Lit 2026-08-26T10:25 PT; crosses the 72h bar 2026-08-29 ~10:25 PT, hence cited now. The alarm's own CDK comment (cdk/stacks/monitoring_prediction_alarms.py:65-73) says it 'fires on the CURRENT corpus the day it deploys (28/50 pending are legacy qualitative rows) and clears as the evaluator retires them at window end (_retire_ungradeable) — deliberate, same posture as #727'. The firing is therefore expected. WHAT IS NOT EXPECTED, and is why this note exists rather than a bare 'deliberate': measured LifePlatform/Predictions daily 2026-08-23..08-26, GradableShare rises 0.3951 / 0.4024 / 0.4024 / 0.4556 while UngradeablePendingCount is FLAT at 49 / 49 / 49 / 49. The share is improving because the GRADABLE numerator is growing, not because legacy rows are being retired. _retire_ungradeable only retires a record once its domain-clamped window has ELAPSED, so a flat 49 is consistent with 'no window has elapsed yet' AND with 'the retirement is not running' — this note does NOT claim to distinguish them, because I did not read the pending corpus out of DynamoDB. That is the open question. RE-DERIVE, do not trust this note: if UngradeablePendingCount is still exactly 49 at the next wrap, the stated clearing mechanism is not the one clearing it and this earns an issue. The 14-day issueless_ancient_reds rule forces a #N by 2026-09-09.

qa-smoke-failures.citation: dated self-clearing state, fix merged — no issue reference, by design. Cause: the deterministic phase-plausibility pass's night floor (rule R7) demanded a night from the FUTURE during the pre-start window, so it raised a high against a CORRECT /api/vitals payload — night_of 2026-08-30 / as_of_date 2026-08-31, which satisfies the platform's own `night_of + 1 == as_of` convention. Fixed 2026-09-01: the floor is now bounded by min(genesis - 1, today - 1), and the fix reaches the qa-smoke Lambda on its next deploy. Expiry: PRUNE this entry once the alarm has been OK longer than the 72h flap window. If it is still lit after the 2026-09-01 nightly run, that is a NEW finding and needs a filed issue.
qa-smoke-failures.note: Added 2026-09-01 (Session P). Deliberately prose rather than an issue reference: the issue that owned this cause is CLOSED because the cause is fixed, and pointing a lit alarm at a closed issue is exactly what the closed-citation rule exists to stop. TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS CLEAR THIS ALARM AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME EVIDENCE — the code fix, and the fact that tonight's sleep record lands night_of = 2026-08-31, which clears even the OLD floor on its own. A green alarm tomorrow is therefore NOT by itself proof the fix worked; the proof is the recorded-payload test table (the launch-eve payload passes, while a two-nights-early payload and the post-start leak both still red). Stated here because the next reader will otherwise read the green as confirmation, and it is not.
